_about: PILOT (read-only): Polity static topics for 'static linking'. Each line is written and checked by hand; the model may only pick ids from this list and never writes static text. Keywords pick candidates for a note.

anchors.label: Article 14
anchors.text: Equality before law and equal protection of the laws.

anchors.label: Article 15
anchors.text: No discrimination on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth; allows special provisions for women, children and backward classes.

anchors.label: Article 16
anchors.text: Equality of opportunity in public employment; allows reservation for backward classes.

anchors.label: Article 19
anchors.text: Six freedoms to citizens, including speech and expression, assembly and movement, subject to reasonable restrictions.

anchors.label: Article 21
anchors.text: Protection of life and personal liberty except by procedure established by law; read by courts to include privacy, dignity, health and a clean environment.

anchors.label: Article 21A
anchors.text: Free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 (86th Amendment, 2002).

anchors.label: Articles 25–28
anchors.text: Freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality and health.

anchors.label: Articles 32 and 226
anchors.text: Right to move the Supreme Court (Art 32) and the High Courts (Art 226) for enforcement of rights through writs.

anchors.label: Article 39A
anchors.text: Equal justice and free legal aid.

anchors.label: Article 40
anchors.text: The State shall organise village panchayats as units of self-government.

anchors.label: Article 44
anchors.text: The State shall endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code for citizens throughout India.

anchors.label: Article 48A
anchors.text: The State shall protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife (42nd Amendment, 1976).

anchors.label: Article 51A
anchors.text: Fundamental duties of citizens (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976, on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation).

anchors.label: Articles 72 and 161
anchors.text: Pardoning powers of the President (Art 72) and the Governor (Art 161).

anchors.label: Articles 74 and 163
anchors.text: A Council of Ministers headed by the PM (Art 74) / CM (Art 163) aids and advises the President / Governor.

anchors.label: Articles 79–81
anchors.text: Parliament consists of the President, the Rajya Sabha (Art 80) and the Lok Sabha (Art 81).

anchors.label: Articles 82 and 170
anchors.text: Readjustment of seats (delimitation) after each census; frozen on the basis of the 1971 census until the first census after 2026.

anchors.label: Article 110
anchors.text: Definition of a Money Bill; the Speaker's decision on it is final and the Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes.

anchors.label: Articles 123 and 213
anchors.text: Ordinance-making power of the President (Art 123) and the Governor (Art 213) when the legislature is not in session.

anchors.label: Article 124 and Article 217
anchors.text: Establishment of the Supreme Court and appointment of Supreme Court (Art 124) and High Court (Art 217) judges; appointments follow the collegium system.

anchors.label: Article 142
anchors.text: The Supreme Court may pass any order necessary for doing complete justice in a matter before it.

anchors.label: Article 143
anchors.text: The President may seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion on a question of law or fact (presidential reference).

anchors.label: Article 148
anchors.text: Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

anchors.label: Articles 153–156
anchors.text: The Governor of a State: appointed by the President and holds office during the President's pleasure.

anchors.label: Article 200
anchors.text: Governor's options on a Bill passed by the State legislature: assent, withhold assent, return it, or reserve it for the President.

anchors.label: Article 239AA
anchors.text: Special provisions for Delhi: an elected Legislative Assembly and Council of Ministers, with police, public order and land outside its powers.

anchors.label: Part IX (Articles 243–243O)
anchors.text: Panchayats: three-tier system, reservation, State Election Commission and State Finance Commission (73rd Amendment, 1992).

anchors.label: Part IXA (Articles 243P–243ZG)
anchors.text: Municipalities (74th Amendment, 1992).

anchors.label: Article 246 and the Seventh Schedule
anchors.text: Division of law-making powers between the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.

anchors.label: Article 262
anchors.text: Parliament may provide for adjudication of inter-State river water disputes.

anchors.label: Article 263
anchors.text: Inter-State Council for coordination between States and the Union.

anchors.label: Article 279A
anchors.text: GST Council of the Union and the States (101st Amendment, 2016).

anchors.label: Article 280
anchors.text: Finance Commission, appointed every five years, recommends the division of taxes between the Union and the States.

anchors.label: Article 312
anchors.text: All-India Services, created by Parliament on a Rajya Sabha resolution.

anchors.label: Articles 315–323
anchors.text: Union and State Public Service Commissions.

anchors.label: Article 324
anchors.text: Superintendence, direction and control of elections are vested in the Election Commission.

anchors.label: Article 326
anchors.text: Elections on the basis of adult suffrage (voting age 18 since the 61st Amendment, 1988).

anchors.label: Articles 338, 338A and 338B
anchors.text: National Commissions for Scheduled Castes (338), Scheduled Tribes (338A) and Backward Classes (338B).

anchors.label: Article 356
anchors.text: President's Rule in a State on failure of constitutional machinery.

anchors.label: Article 368
anchors.text: Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and the procedure for it.

anchors.label: Article 370
anchors.text: Temporary provision for Jammu and Kashmir; made inoperative in August 2019, a move upheld by the Supreme Court in December 2023.

anchors.label: Fifth Schedule
anchors.text: Administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes, with Tribes Advisory Councils.

anchors.label: Sixth Schedule
anchors.text: Autonomous District Councils for tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

anchors.label: Eighth Schedule
anchors.text: The 22 languages recognised by the Constitution.

anchors.label: Tenth Schedule
anchors.text: Anti-defection law (52nd Amendment, 1985); the Speaker or Chairman decides disqualification.

anchors.label: 103rd Amendment, 2019
anchors.text: Up to 10% reservation for economically weaker sections in education and public jobs; upheld by the Supreme Court in 2022.

anchors.label: 106th Amendment, 2023
anchors.text: One-third of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies reserved for women, to take effect after delimitation following the next census.

anchors.label: Representation of the People Act, 1951
anchors.text: Conduct of elections, qualifications and disqualifications of members, and election disputes.

anchors.label: Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)
anchors.text: Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution but not its basic structure.

anchors.label: Maneka Gandhi case (1978)
anchors.text: Procedure that takes away life or liberty must be fair, just and reasonable; Articles 14, 19 and 21 are linked.

anchors.label: S.R. Bommai case (1994)
anchors.text: President's Rule is open to judicial review, majority is tested on the floor of the House, and secularism is part of the basic structure.

anchors.label: Indra Sawhney case (1992)
anchors.text: Upheld OBC reservation, excluded the creamy layer and set a 50% ceiling on reservations save in exceptional cases.

anchors.label: K.S. Puttaswamy case (2017)
anchors.text: Privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21 and Part III.

anchors.label: Vishaka case (1997)
anchors.text: Guidelines against sexual harassment at the workplace, later replaced by the POSH Act, 2013.

anchors.label: Shayara Bano case (2017)
anchors.text: Instant triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) held unconstitutional.

anchors.label: Navtej Singh Johar case (2018)
anchors.text: Consensual same-sex relations between adults decriminalised by reading down Section 377 IPC.

anchors.label: Electoral bonds case (2024)
anchors.text: The Supreme Court struck down the electoral bond scheme in February 2024 as violating voters' right to information.

anchors.label: Lily Thomas case (2013)
anchors.text: MPs and MLAs convicted of certain offences are disqualified at once; Section 8(4) of the RPA, 1951 was struck down.

anchors.label: Second Judges case (1993) and NJAC case (2015)
anchors.text: Collegium primacy in judicial appointments; the National Judicial Appointments Commission was struck down in 2015.
